functional.reason: Functional results ARE committed (see evals/functional/), but the skill-eval harness provisions throwaway agent spaces with no injected broken resources, so the output-assertion checks cannot pass regardless of skill quality. Trigger detection is reliable for 4 of the 5 evals.json scenarios; the committed v2 run itself shows the exception - cross-account-share-invisible failed the automated trigger check in 2 of 3 with_skill iterations (skill_loads_found: 0). That scenario also cannot be fully exercised manually in this sandbox: it needs a genuine second AWS account to accept a real cross-account RAM share, which this single-account test environment does not have, so it has never been manually diagnosed end to end in any round. A 4-trial activation-only check (no AWS resources required, since recognizing a prompt as relevant doesn't depend on real backing data) found the skill correctly recognized as relevant in all 4 trials, with some run-to-run variance in whether it engaged the skill directly or via an extra orchestrator-level delegation step first - see the PR description's Testing section for the full 4-trial detail. The other 4 scenarios were each manually diagnosed end to end, once, against independently verified ground truth, and passed; attached to the pull request. This exemption flags the tool-assertion limitation; remove it once the harness supports injecting broken resources into functional eval spaces.
